tasks.spec:
You are writing a test-first specification in freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. No network, no model call, no uv: `export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp`, run `.venv/bin/python`. Do not git commit. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: tests/test_observation_context.py (new). Never edit storygame/, packages/, data/, docs/, .plans/. Do NOT create storygame/runtime/observation.py: the tests describe it before it exists.

READ FIRST: .plans/grounded-llm-environment-narration.md sections 'Required architecture' 1-3 and the 'Regression matrix' table; .plans/grounded-llm-environment-narration/t2-visibility-audit.md (what worldkeeper can and cannot say about sight); packages/worldkeeper/src/worldkeeper/model.py (World, WorldSchema.from_data, is_visible, is_shut_away, given_with, holder, place_label, contents, reveal, set_axis, move); packages/worldkeeper/tests/test_world.py and test_seats.py (how to build a World from a schema dict); tests/test_seating.py (how existing tests load the real 1A package and move things). Rule for every test input: authored player commands are imperative ('Enter the truck.', 'Inspect the passenger seat.', 'Examine my laptop.'), first-person possessives for the player's own things.

THE API UNDER TEST (new, story-agnostic, pure; built on a worldkeeper World, never on a story package): `from storygame.runtime.observation import ObservationRequest, ObservationContext, ObservedThing, ObservationScopeTooLarge, build_observation_context`. `ObservationRequest(action: str, kind: 'look'|'open'|'enter'|'none', focus: str|None)`; focus is an engine entity id and kind is a typed value from the existing intent proposal, never derived from verbs by the module. `build_observation_context(world, observer_id, request, completed_actions=(), max_required=8, max_optional=8) -> ObservationContext`, frozen. Fields: `observer` (public name), `action` (the ORIGINAL player action string, unchanged), `completed_actions` (tuple[str]: implicit steps already done, kept separate from action), `visible_things` (tuple[ObservedThing] with public `name`, `place` (public label like 'passenger seat'), `holder` (public name or None)), `contingent_things` (what an opening action would expose; empty unless kind == 'open'), `required` (tuple of public names that must be described), `omitted_optional` (tuple of names dropped for budget), `scope_complete` (bool; False unless the world declares completeness), and `prompt_fields() -> dict[str, object]` holding only strings/lists of strings/bools. ObservationScopeTooLarge is raised when required names exceed max_required; optional detail is dropped first.

WRITE tests/test_observation_context.py with these groups. (A) FIXTURE SANITY, plain tests that MUST PASS NOW and only use worldkeeper and the real package: for every case below, assert the world facts the case relies on (who holds what, which container is closed, what is hidden, which place a thing is on), so a later failure can only come from the missing module. Include three tests that demonstrate the audit's gaps with today's API: is_visible of the truck's laptop is the same True from outside the truck and from the driver's seat; an emptied container and a never-described container are indistinguishable through contents(); given_with of a closed container returns its shut-away contents together with visible ones. (B) PROJECTION TESTS, one per row, each marked with a module-level `needs_projection = pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, raises=ImportError, reason='T3 implements storygame.runtime.observation')`; import the module INSIDE a helper function called from the test body so the failure is ImportError, never collection error; one assertion group per behavior: 1 'Enter the truck.' (kind enter, completed_actions holds the seating step, observer seated, the laptop is in visible_things with place 'passenger seat' and in required, action text unchanged and not duplicated into completed_actions, no entity ids anywhere in prompt_fields()); 2 'Approach the truck.' (kind none, outside: laptop NOT in required and not in visible_things); 3 'Inspect the passenger seat.' after the observer carries the laptop elsewhere (laptop not listed on the seat, no stale seat label); 4 'Examine my laptop.' after carrying it to another room (one entry, holder is the observer, place not the seat); 5 'Open the drawer.' with a public item and a hidden story item inside (public item in contingent_things, hidden item absent from every field and from prompt_fields()); 6 'Inspect the closed drawer.' (kind look, contents in neither visible_things nor required, nothing contingent); 7 'Search beneath the drawer.' after the item was recovered (the held item never reappears as a thing under the drawer); 8 'Enter the truck and inspect my laptop.' (action text preserved whole, completed_actions has the implicit step once, laptop required); 9 'Examine the kitchen.' (a thing in another area and a thing only in the referring text never enter visible_things); 10 synthetic observatory: a World built from a schema dict with no Kristin vocabulary and no notice text, 'Inspect the telescope tray.' (a lens on the tray is required and placed at 'telescope tray'); 11 synthetic skiff: 'Board the skiff.' with differently named cargo and seats gives the same shape of result without any code change; 12 budget: required items over max_required raise ObservationScopeTooLarge and are never silently dropped, while optional extras beyond max_optional are dropped and reported in omitted_optional; 13 determinism: the same world and request produce equal contexts twice; 14 safety: prompt_fields() holds no entity id, no hidden or shut-away name, and is JSON-serialisable. (C) SCHEMA-NEED TESTS for the two audit gaps, also xfail(strict=True, raises=(ImportError, SchemaError)) with SchemaError from worldkeeper: 15 'Look through the truck window.' with an unobstructed declared view the laptop is visible from outside the truck while the observer stays outside, and with the view blocked (`blocked_by` axis pole holding) it is withheld; 16 a container declaring contents_complete true and empty gives scope_complete True and no known contents, while an undeclared container gives scope_complete False. Declare these with the keys named in the audit doc (`view`: list of {from, blocked_by}; `contents_complete`: bool) in the schema dict you pass to WorldSchema.from_data. Build the real-package cases (1-9) from data/stories/continuity-initiative exactly as tests/test_seating.py does (load_story_package, RuntimeState.bootstrap, world_for); discover real ids with the world's own queries, do not hardcode a guess without asserting it in group A.

Tests must not need a worker, network or a model. Keep the file focused (no helpers beyond what the cases need). FINISH: run the file, then `ruff check` and `ruff format` on it. Report in your final message the counts of passed and xfailed and any case you could not express.
tasks.check: cd /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge && export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp && set -o pipefail && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov -rx tests/test_observation_context.py 2>&1 | tee /tmp/env-t2.out | tail -30 && grep -Eq '[0-9]+ xfailed' /tmp/env-t2.out && ! grep -Eq '[0-9]+ (failed|error)' /tmp/env-t2.out && .venv/bin/python -c "import re;t=open('/tmp/env-t2.out').read();p=int(re.search(r'(\d+) passed',t).group(1));x=int(re.search(r'(\d+) xfailed',t).group(1));assert p>=4,('passed',p);assert x>=16,('xfailed',x);print('passed',p,'xfailed',x)" && grep -c 'strict=True' tests/test_observation_context.py && ! grep -E 'xfail\(' tests/test_observation_context.py | grep -v 'strict=True' && test ! -e storygame/runtime/observation.py && git diff --quiet -- storygame packages data docs worker && .venv/bin/python -m ruff check tests/test_observation_context.py && .venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check tests/test_observation_context.py
